evals.prompt: If I want to implement a feature with you, what will you do with me? Which skill or workflow do you use?
evals.expected_output: Calls atlas search (and get) for how a feature is organised in this project before describing the workflow; the workflow it describes names an atlas call at each step it depends on (search for conventions, symbol before an import, presets for a new app or package); it does not claim an atlas lookup it has not made; nothing is written or committed

evals.prompt: Add a GET endpoint that returns the server time to the first backend app. Propose the surface first; do not write code yet.
evals.expected_output: Calls atlas search for how a controller and a route are written here and get on the hits; proposes the route, its response schema and the controller and method names, each convention backed by the atlas hit it came from; waits for approval; no source file changed

evals.prompt: We need a second backend app named billing and a shared library named money. Set them up.
evals.expected_output: Calls atlas presets, then runs the exact vulcan add commands it returned (an app with --app billing, a library with --lib money); never hand-writes a package.json, a tsconfig or scripts; runs the new packages' checks and vulcan doctor; nothing committed
